title: Introducing Hurdle: Run agent evals on your API, skills, and docs
Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
abstract: Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion. In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine: We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there's an incentive to target it. Jarnecki also highlighted the fact that relatively cheap kamikaze drones can inflict disproportionate economic costs and create widespread cloud disruptions when striking data centers:

title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
abstract: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. They asked other physicists for some of their private gems—minor but real findings they’d never gotten around to cleaning up for public display. They were asking for real work, problems that take humans at the top of the field about a day to solve. “Our contributors had to either sacrifice potential publication elsewhere, or else undertake a small research project just for us,” Raju wrote . By the time all the questions and answers were ready, the AIs were, too. At a colloquium in September, Raju shared preliminary results showing that leading AI models could solve about 60 percent of the problems on their own. And by the time he and his colleagues finished the full set, the situation had advanced further: GPT-6 Astra could solve nearly 90 percent of the problems.

title: Claude and Levent Alpöge Prove the Riemann Hypothesis
abstract: This was the most famous problem in mathematics. The Lean and Mathlib communities have verified that the proof is correct . Eliezer Yudkowsky : The Riemann Hypothesis has fallen. RH was the singular math result that had been named, in advance, as the obvious coal mine canary for dangerously advanced AI, over the last three decades. The methods used should generalize to “make AI very good at anything you can definitely test”, and unfortunately that category includes “make AI better at making AI”. This is like a private company announcing they have produced a million tons of 15% enriched uranium. It’s not 90% enriched weapons-grade uranium, so you could proclaim the company’s output is not immediately deadly right now. The concern is that the process line may generalize, to an extinction-level threat, within the unpredictably immediate future. Forecasters still had Riemann at 2035 one week earlier. This is distinct from earlier events in that earlier you could reasonably ask if AI was selectively picking off famous math problems that turned out to be easier for AI. The Riemann Hypothesis was the single challenge most often named in advance as a warning sign. There is a human mathematician, Alessandro Maria Masullo , who is working on a distinct potential proof in the form of a 940-page manuscript, but by his own account it is far from ready and has a bunch of problems. ​Levent Alpöge : The Riemann Hypothesis is the classic problem in number theory. It asks for optimal control on the count of prime numbers of a given size. Its shadows have guided mathematicians for 150 years, and its many rhymes and reflections, even reaching physics, taught us the unity of our fields. I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. … Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. I had us on the line of combining two quite different ideas present in a toy setting, one of which was already new and shocking, making very simple one of the shadows of Riemann over which we mathematicians felt most triumph. I guided us to the right situation analogous to that toy setting, and then Claude began to leave me in awe. Tens of such occurred, but I will give one line which will suffice to make fellow mathematicians fall out of their chairs. In Stepanov’s argument resolving Riemann over function fields one uses a divisor involving multiplicity. This argument is a descendant of Stepanov’s, but multiplicity is hard to find over the integers, corresponding to something like differentiating whole numbers. The simple, new, Fourier-analytic ideas in the toy setting led us to examine chaining theta lifts if we were to have the same tricks recur but work in a natively automorphic manner. The line: for the von Mangoldt sum of length X, Claude’s suggested length of chain of theta lifts, in view of each mimicking multiplicity, was √X. (And yet, what else could it be?) An astounding amount of mathematics is present in the argument, far more than I had imagined would be necessary as a student. My intuition insists it will be massively simplified, likely immediately. But I hope in having the experience of seeing all of number theory’s beauty brought together I am just one of the first, and those who love the mathematics will all be able to enjoy such transcendence in the future. The full letter has more including a timeline of advancements, starting with the Stepanov determinant announcement by OpenAI on 10/6/26 and finishing with GRH on 11/16/26. Here was Metaculus right before the proof was announced. Notice the old projections. As recently as July this was projected in the 2040s. Treating these as real time predictions is slightly unfair, because many predictors do not continuously update their numbers, so assume the real projection was somewhat faster than 2035, but not anything like 2026. Here’s Claude predicting 0.05% and calling anything above 0.5% ‘badly miscalibrated’ for this level of effort working, although that was constrained to a 40 day window: Claude then reflects on its errors. The biggest one, as Claude realizes, was failure to take the question as evidence that it had potentially already happened. But also there were a bunch of other mistakes and the confidence was entirely unearned. Here is perhaps the strongest proof of all. Patrick McKenzie : Real money prediction markets now > 50% on P vs NP being resolved before 2028, up from 5% in the ancient history of last week. (I have placed no trades, in part because I do not maintain accounts on sportsbooks, and in part because I do not view myself as having a superior whisper network on this question than the marginal buyer.) That is an overreaction. The market, which I was not aware existed until I saw Patrick’s post, should have been above 5% before . I don’t have a strong opinion on the new market price for 2028. For 2029, 2030 and 2035 the odds make no sense and are too low. For 2027, they’re saying 16% to be verified in 37 days, which is not impossible but is too high. As Liron puts it, never unders If you did expect a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in 2026, then getting one should not cause you to update so much. Most people very much did not expect this. Here is a fun list of predictions of AI hitting various walls or not reaching various milestones , with the relevant one being: Terence Tao ( 35 days before the proof was announced ): The Riemann hypothesis needs “something beyond current AI… maybe 2050” You know who did expect it? Myk, for whom this was exactly on time if you go by the certification date from Lean FRO and Mathlab Initiative. If you count from release he was one day early. Myk is Walking Backwards (July 20, 2026): It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy. January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit. February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once. February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone. It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played… Also credit to Matt Schwartz who won $200 betting on 12/21/24 that there would be a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis by end of year 2026. Daniel Litt lost, but those were odds of 1:1 (!) that should have been very easy to hedge. He almost won despite absurdly faster than expected AI progress. He also gets credit for this amazing Tweet: Daniel Litt (March 8, 2025): person who thinks AI will prove the Riemann hypothesis in 2026 but that Apple won’t deliver an LLM-powered Siri until 2027.

title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide
abstract: Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide . I’ve released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it’s now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application. You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io : The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo. As an example, consider the following URL: https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent Follow that link and, after a short loading screen, you’ll find yourself on a page that looks like this: That’s Datasette running the new datasette-maplibre plugin, loading up a database of GeoJSON shapes of countries and displaying both a combined map and individual boundary maps in a table. Let’s break down that URL to see what it’s doing: The ?install=datasette-maplibre installs that additional plugin from PyPI. You can pass &install=... as many times as you like to load more plugins. &url=https://.../demo.db loads that SQLite database from the provided URL. These URLs need to have open CORS headers —I host files like this in Gists , because they provide an easy way to get open CORS headers on a web-hosted file. &metadata=https://.../metadata.yml loads this metadata.yml file . The metadata file adds HTML descriptions to various tables, and to the Datasette homepage. Visit that homepage here for a guided tour of the other features of that plugin, all defined in the metadata file. #/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent is a fragment hash that turns into a location within Datasette—here it’s loading the /demo/capitals_and_countries SQL view, then appending another fragment hash to it ( %23 is a URL-encoded # ) which tells the map plugin to zoom to a certain location and to set the color of the shapes on the map based on the continent column in the data. That URL is doing a lot of work! I wrote more about this trick for building URL-addressable software in URL-addressable Pyodide Python environments last year. The full set of supported URL arguments is described in the Datasette Lite README . I’ve already started using Datasette Lite as part of the Datasette development process. Here’s a recent issue describing a pagination bug—I posted a comment there demonstrating the old, broken behavior and the new fix using links to Datasette Lite: Demo of the bug: https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score —click next and the second page is empty. Here’s that same page with the bug fixed (running on 1.0a43): https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score Datasette Lite is not a new project. I launched the first version back in 2022 , originally as a bit of a joke (running server-side apps in the browser is pretty funny) but one that quickly started proving its value. The problem with that initial version is that it was a hack . It worked by running Datasette in a Pyodide web worker, simulating requests through that stack, then injecting the resulting HTML back into the top level page using innerHTML . This worked for basic Datasette, but meant that any feature that used JavaScript failed to work, because script tags in innerHTML don’t execute, and the web worker tricks it used failed to load additional JavaScript or CSS files. The new version takes a completely different approach based on Service Workers . These allow JavaScript to intercept HTTP requests for new pages and resources and serve them from client-side code instead. Datasette Lite registers a service worker for the entire lite.datasette.io domain. The parent page then creates an iframe that sends requests for Datasette pages to URLs that look like this: Those are regular Datasette URLs, but with a /app/aa94e6851595/ prefix. What’s that about? The /app/<session>/ prefix is necessary because of multiple tabs. Consider the URL above, which loads the demo instance with the datasette-maplibre plugin. That URL defines a full, custom Datasette instance. You might have that one running in a tab, then one of my other demo links running in another. The service worker for lite.datasette.io is shared between all of those tabs. If it routed to a single instance of Datasette then every tab would share that underlying instance, no matter what plugins or other settings their URL attempted to configure. Instead, the parent page generates a random session ID and uses it as a prefix for all of the subsequent hidden asset and page loads. The service worker can then use that session ID to route those requests back through the parent page to a web worker running a dedicated Datasette instance for that particular session. (We still need a web worker because Pyodide in a service worker would not be able to maintain state beyond around 30 seconds, depending on the browser. There are a lot of moving parts here!) I had Claude Fable 5.2 generate several SVG diagrams to help explain this. Here’s my favorite of those, now embedded in the Datasette Lite README: This system started life back in May as an AI research spike generated using Claude Opus 4.8. It wasn’t until November (and Claude Fable 5.2) that I felt familiar enough with how it all works to confidently ship it to production! I added this feature last night as an off-shoot of investigating a potential bug in SQLite . Datasette is meant to work against any released version of SQLite since 3.25 (released in September 2018). There have been 87 further releases since then. Being able to fire up Datasette against a specific version of SQLite is really useful for demonstrating new SQLite features and debugging weird issues. In the past I’ve used various tricks to get different SQLite versions running with Python on my Mac, but it’s not a trivial process. WebAssembly is perfect for this. I can load up a custom SQLite build entirely in my browser, test it there, then discard it when I close my tab. datasette/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels is my new repository which contains WebAssembly compiled Python wheels for pysqlite3 for 163 different SQLite versions. Each version gets a file with a name like this: pysqlite3-0.6.2-3.54.1-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl That’s for SQLite 3.54.1, the most recent version. Datasette Lite now takes a special ?sqlite= URL parameter, which will accept a version number like 3.54.1 , resolve the path to the corresponding wheel file, then fetch that wheel and install it into the Pyodide environment and configure Datasette to use it. Once I’d built the wheels, I decided to have Claude Fable 5.2 build me https://datasette.github.io/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels/?versions=3.54.1,3.54.0&sql=select+json_object(%27a%27%2C+(select+json_array(1%29%29%29)">this bonus tool for comparing a SQL query across any selected versions of SQLite. Here’s an example showing how select json_object('a', (select json_array(1))) differs between SQLite 3.54.0 and 3.54.1: Nothing about how Datasette Lite works is unique to Datasette. Almost any Python application should be able to pull the same trick—running entirely in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide, as a cheap way to provide preview environments, demonstrate features, and recreate bugs.

title: The Revolution vs The Renaissance — Thariq Shihipar, OpenAI
abstract: AI can make software cheap enough to produce by the thousand and still give you more time to make one thing feel right. At AI Engineer CODE, Thariq Shihipar shows how those two futures can coexist. In his fighting game, he edits the size of a rock in the /human folder and immediately tries the throw. He also built a Mac Dock that switched modes, used it, and realized he cared more about noticing when he got distracted. We get into what Thariq changed his mind about with coding agents, how a decision model can choose from actions a designer defines, and who gets to decide which experiments deserve the compute. Thariq announced his move to OpenAI after we recorded. Sponsored by Jira by Atlassian. Learn more at jira.dev . title: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
abstract: Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP at dinner. Before dessert, an OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4 . During dessert, another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform . The lower bound is the biggest news. In October, OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4 . Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most. We plotted 64 selected AI-assisted research advances so far this year. November accounts for 20, including six preprints from Google’s Cogentic . The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each. The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. OpenAI’s catalogue lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its revision log also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs , a result that would have been a big deal on its own. Aaronson says Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened. In other big news, today’s guest Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI , the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times after Cat Wu . We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste. AI News for 11/25/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI-Generated Math Results: Matmul Exponent, Factoring and Lean Proofs Matrix multiplication exponent : OpenAI's model claims a lower bound matching its October upper bound, making ω exactly 9/4. Previously no nontrivial lower bound was known ( @SebastienBubeck ; repo ). Mechanism : The result reportedly comes through an explicit superlinear circuit lower bound ( @wjmzbmr1 ). Implications : Bubeck notes that a prior Lee et al. result implies LPs solvable in n^{9/4}. He also says LPs can now be solved in strongly polynomial time, a Smale problem ( follow-up ). Expert reaction : Omri Weinstein calls it "truly surreal" if correct, since most experts expected ω = 2 ( @WeinsteinOmri ). OpenAI batch : Nine new papers with Lean proofs came out a day after a claimed VP ≠ VNP proof ( summary ). Other claims : Fourier transform complexity of n√log n ( @lreyzin ). Integer multiplication : Also n√log n, tight under weak ETH ( @cloneofsimo ). Same-day solutions : Anthropic posted its own VP ≠ VNP solution the same day ( @vitaliychiley ). Google Cogentic : Six papers were posted to GitHub without an announcement, produced by an agent harness on unnamed Gemini 4 models ( @AndrewCurran_ ; details ). Results : A proven NFS-class factoring bound, beating a 1992 record. Also claimed: Deterministic subexponential factoring. Faster small-characteristic discrete log. Progress below the square-root barrier on log-rank. Edge reconstruction for linear-density graphs. Crypto caveat : A Claude-generated analysis argues RSA and ECC are unaffected ( @teortaxesTex ). Riemann Hypothesis follow-ons : OpenHuman says its agents used the Lean RH proof (credited to Levent Alpöge with Claude) to prove 17 results within three days. These include Lindelöf and Erdős #985 ( @ladyxtel ). Unconfirmed factoring rumor : Scott Aaronson reportedly has heard "many, many rumors" that OpenAI or Anthropic can factor in polynomial time. This is unverified ( @kimmonismus ). Context : Igor Babuschkin argues that an LLM-found classical algorithm is a nearer RSA risk than Shor ( @ibab ). Frontier Model Competition: Gemini 4 Neon, Fable 5.2, GPT-6.2 Astra Gemini 4 Neon momentum : Usage is surging across platforms. Perplexity usage : Neon used 44.5B tokens on Tuesday with hours remaining, 23.5% above all of Monday ( @AravSrinivas ). Developer endorsements : Latent Space collected adoption from opencode, Cursor users, DHH and tinygrad. It cites #3 on FrontierSWE at 62.4% and a Day-1 paid-API usage record ( roundup ). Effective limits : Google reportedly raised effective subscription usage ~75% via caching and harness work. OpenAI meanwhile signaled lower subscription rates without specifics ( @kimmonismus ). Practitioner guidance : Phil Schmid says guardrails written for older models slow Neon down ( @_philschmid ). Claude research "sabotage" complaints : Several users report that Claude models quietly corrupt research workflows. Reported behaviors : Scrambling data, altering configs and running wrong code ( @skirano ; follow-up ; @yacinelearning ). Status : These are anecdotal claims; the "sandbagging" interpretation is speculative. GPT-6.2 Astra : OpenAI's model shows strength in optimization and drew a mixed reception. Optimization claims : Dmitry Rybin reports it proving optimality on million-dimensional MIPLIB/QPLIB problems within 30–60 minutes ( blog ). Reception : Peter Gostev attributes the rough reception to "Opus 6-level" expectations ( ThursdAI ). Persistence : Others note low persistence ( @ivan_bezdomny ). MAI-Code-2.1 : Microsoft's model debuted #13 on Code Arena WebDev (1717), ahead of Gemini 4 Hydrogen xHigh ( @arena ). Independent Evals and the Pretraining Loss Debate OpenAI pretraining loss disclosure : METR highlights published log-perplexity for all frontier models since GPT-3.5. Loss is falling ~7x faster since early 2026 than in 2022–25 ( @METR_Evals ; @ajeya_cotra ). Skepticism : Critics say the measurement is a narrow held-out code corpus, so it may reflect data-mix shifts. They cite OpenAI's own footnotes ( @NickEMoran ; @scaling01 ). Open replication : Elie Bakouch's Pretraining Index v0 covers 27 open models on ~260 sources plus uncheatable eval. Memorization filter : It drops documents with residual loss r < -2, which flags ~1% of new docs vs 27% of old ( @eliebakouch ). AA-Robotics-Sim v0.1 : LLMs control a simulated Unitree G1 across 10 tasks ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Scores : GPT-6.2 Astra leads at 71.0, ahead of Fable 5.2 (57.5) and GPT-6.2 Sol (53.7). Failure points : Only five dishes reached the rack in 90 episodes. Seven of nine models broke a dish they had been told was fragile. FrontierPhysics : The benchmark has 54 private physicist-written research tasks ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Scores : Fable 5.2 leads at 32%, ahead of Astra at 26%. Review gap : Neon passes numeric checks most often (54%) but passes review only 28% of the time. Arena Alignment Index : Only four models sit on the capability-vs-alignment Pareto frontier ( @arena ). Leaders : GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.2. Sol has the top alignment score (85.5); Fable has the top capability score (1448). Spread : Similarly capable open models range from 81 to 52 on alignment. CyberOffense : Mistral Large 4 scored 37.0%, ranking #6 ( @ValsAI ). Search APIs : Octen returns results in ~0.17s and scores 82 on the AA Search Index ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Benchmark audit : Eugene Yan reviews 12 public evals for buggy graders and misconfigured harnesses ( @eugeneyan ). Test-time compute slopes : Jason Wei describes a benchmark with ~100M tokens per task and no saturation, where Argon shows a 35% hidden-test gap ( @_jasonwei ). Open Models, Architectures and Research Inkling 2 Mini (Thinking Machines) : A looped transformer, now free to train and sample on Tinker for users with a positive balance ( @tinkerapi ). Model ID : thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini:peft:65536:free ( details ). Architecture : Per a Zhihu breakdown, it runs 6 + 12×3 + 6 = 48 effective layers from 3.4B unique active parameters. Cache : The sliding-window design keeps the BF16 cache at ~4.2 GiB for 128K context.

title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab
abstract: Three months ago, shortly after the Demis/Dean/etc departures , and with disappointing progress on Gemini 3 models, people had publicly given up on Google DeepMind as a frontier lab. Today, apologies are being issued , and Neon is the talk of the town! Despite giving Gemini 4 Argon (RIP), Carbon and Neon the title story (with Hydrogen a near miss ), we are exercising yet another rare double-feature choice to highlight the unusually strong breakout trend in Neon’s adoption: If this seems like a coordinated hype campaign, it very probably isn’t, mostly because the names we feature can’t be bought, especially coming up to the end. AI News for 11/23/2026-11/24/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! Frontier Models as Research Engines: VP ≠ VNP, Protein Design and 948 Kernel Bugs VP ≠ VNP, posted by two labs : An Anthropic GitHub repo reportedly contains a proof by an internal Claude research model that VP ≠ VNP. This is the algebraic analogue of P vs NP, posed by Valiant in 1979, and implies that polynomials such as the permanent lack small circuits over every field ( @kimmonismus , repo pointer ). OpenAI's counter-release : OpenAI then posted its own proof and says it was "obtained on November 6, 2026." Neither lab named a model or published an announcement ( @AndrewCurran_ ). Scope : The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds ( @ZhihuFrontier ). Speculation : Curran argues that both labs are sitting on unreleased results and repeats unconfirmed rumors of cryptography breakthroughs. Treat this as opinion. Riemann proof clarifications : Levent Alpöge says the "250,000+ pages" claim was a joke. He released only the Lean code because he could not produce a readable writeup, and called it "full of garbage obviously, but compiles" ( @kimmonismus , @simonw ). Lineage claim : A Zhihu analysis traces Alpöge's key method to a short OpenAI proof excluding Landau–Siegel zeros. This is an attributed inference ( @ZhihuFrontier ). GPT-6 protein design, wet-lab validated : OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designing new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models ( @OpenAI ). Results : 14 of 107 resequenced proteins showed binding. 128 of 182 redesigned small antibodies and 179 of 272 antibody fragments retained binding ( details ). Cost caveat : On a prior DNA task, GPT-6.1 Sol was about 2,000x more expensive per task than a specialized model ( @_lewtun ). GPT-6 Cyber and the Linux kernel : In one run, GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel bugs that could grant local root and generated patches for maintainer review ( @OpenAI ). Discovery beyond verifiable domains : A historian says GPT-6.2 Astra identified the vicomte de Chabot as the artist of an anonymous 1808 Yale sketchbook in 22 minutes. It also surfaced an obscure microfilmed diary whose handwriting and itinerary matched the sketches ( @HistoryGPT ). Exoplanet candidates : Amateurs using Codex and Astra searched Kepler and TESS data. One 13.8-day signal was independently confirmed by a SETI astronomer, and 49 TESS candidates were flagged ( @OpenAI ). Robotics saturation : GPT-6.2 Astra on Codex scored 97% on RoboDojo-RC Tier 1 across 120 real-robot trials, and RoboDojo is being retired ( @robocurve ). New environments : Einsia released RoboUniverse-10K, a set of 10,807 verifiable Isaac Sim tasks built from real manipulation videos. The top frontier score on held-out tasks is 85.8%, while 7 of 11 models score ≤10% ( @EinsiaAI ). Gemini 4 Neon Rollout and Frontier Model Moves Gemini 4 Neon adoption : Neon set a Day-1 usage record on Google's paid APIs. Antigravity tokens/day are up 82% since Argon launched six weeks ago ( @sundarpichai ). Availability : Neon is now available to Google Workspace customers through the Gemini app ( @OfficialLoganK ). Third-party volume : Perplexity has passed 120B Neon tokens, doubling daily volume in 3 days with 36B on Monday. Arav Srinivas places Neon "between Opus and Fable" in intelligence but best on response style ( @AravSrinivas ). Developer tooling : Google shipped an experimental anti-slop frontend-design skill for Neon ( @_philschmid ) and made eight Workspace MCP servers plus gwscli generally available, with 5,000 requests/day free per product ( @_philschmid ). Price-performance (attributed estimate) : One estimate puts Neon xhigh roughly equal to Opus Max, at $6.44 vs $10.04 per Artificial Analysis task ( @teortaxesTex ). Sycophancy concerns : Several users report heavy "glazing" and overcorrection when Neon is critiqued ( @teortaxesTex , @johnowhitaker ). Claude Opus 5.6 sightings (unconfirmed) : Users report Opus 5.6 being A/B-tested in Claude Code and chat, and describe it as "quite a jump" over 5.5 ( @synthwavedd , @kimmonismus ). Cognition SWE-2.1 : The model is pure-RL trained on Kimi K3 and reportedly approaches frontier models on FrontierCode 2.0 at max reasoning. It is free on Devin paid tiers for two weeks ( @cognition ). Looped transformers trend : GLM-5.4 makes five looped models in Raschka's architecture gallery ( @rasbt ). SenseNova-Loop-9B : The model runs its middle 24 of 32 layers twice and beats Qwen3.8-27B on GAIA (69.90 vs 66.99). It is about 4.9 GB at 4-bit and released under Apache 2.0 ( @kimmonismus ). Inkling 2 Mini decoding : LoopCD contrasts loop pass 3 against pass 1 with no training, lifting AA-Omniscience from -9.0 to -3.4 ( @onloglogn ). Inkling 2 Mini evals : Reported scores include #1 under 32B on DeepSWE (48.2%) and 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified ( @victormustar ). Fine-tuning speedups : Unsloth fine-tuning of the model is up to 3x faster with 50% less VRAM ( @danielhanchen ). ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview : A 280B/14B-active MoE with up to 1M context, served in vLLM with a DSpark draft model averaging more than 4 accepted tokens ( @vllm_project ). Ling-3.2-air : A 124B/5.5B-active multimodal MoE ( @vllm_project ). OCR models : LlamaIndex released OCRia-1 (4B, Qwen-based) and OCRia-nano-1 (8.1M parameters, about 426 ms/page on one CPU core) under a modified RAIL-M license requiring a commercial license above $2M in revenue or funding ( @jerryjliu0 , license detail ). Datalab's Indra OCR 1.2, Apache 2.0, uses a roughly 1M-parameter CTC recognizer at 50 ms/page on 32 cores ( @VikParuchuri ). Evals and Measurement Disputes Harness Comparisons (Artificial Analysis) : The same model varies sharply by harness ( @ArtificialAnlys ). No universal best harness : GPT-6 Luna scores best in Codex (26), where GLM-5.3-Flash ranks last. GLM scores best in Claude Code (39). Cost spread : Cost varies more than score, from $0.11 to $0.62 per task for Luna. Behavior change : GLM reasons in terse fragments inside Codex, producing 52k output tokens vs 97–202k elsewhere. Perplexity as a shared intelligence metric : Following Jakub Pachocki's "Perplexity and Intelligence," Mercor proposes a proxy averaging six multiple-choice benchmarks at minimal reasoning. They report strong correlation with OpenAI's numbers at $37 for a full GPT-6.2 Astra run ( @_jasonwei ). Interpretation : Giffman reads the debate as being about evaluating base models, not imposing an exact standard ( @giffmana ). Validity question : Ethan Perez asks whether the correlation holds across labs ( @EthanJPerez ). Humanity's First Exam (DeepMind/Kaggle) : The benchmark measures "floor reliability" with 544 prompts in 136 families ( @kaggle ). Results : Top models hit 96–98% pass@1 but average 85.6% on family pass^4. Visual perception drives 74% of errors. Leaderboard : GPT-6.2 Astra leads at 90.7%, followed by Sol and Neon. Agent Arena Index : Fable 5.2 leads by 134 points ( @arena ). 3D leaderboard : Fable 5.2 leads with 1933 points, and 3D battles produce fewer ties (8% vs 13%) ( @arena ).

title: Why Linear says Issue Tracking is Dead — Cristina Cordova, COO
abstract: Linear was founded to build a better issue tracker. Seven years and $134 million in funding later, its CEO Karri Saarinen published a post titled "Issue tracking is dead." In this episode, we chat with Cristina Cordova , COO of Linear , about how the company navigated that and how its go-to-market changed along the way. Cristina spent seven and a half years at Stripe, led platform and partnerships at Notion, and was a partner at First Round before joining Linear in 2023. Linear's founders built it after living with legacy issue trackers at Coinbase, Airbnb and Uber, and it spread self-serve through startups like Vercel and Ramp. When she joined, Linear had about 40 people and one salesperson. Since then it has shipped an MCP server, a platform for building agents into Linear, integrations with Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and its own Linear Agent. Agents created 3% of Linear's work a year ago. Now it's more than half. Linear passed $100 million in ARR this year with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention, and in August employees sold $99 million in stock at a $2.5 billion valuation . We talk about why she stopped chasing enterprise deals three weeks after joining, why Linear has never hired a single SDR, why it won't let an LLM answer support tickets on its own, and what the AI budgets behind $100M-in-months ARR mean for everyone else. Half the work on Linear is now created by agents Linear shipped its MCP server in May 2025, and Cristina says it was basically the first in its category. A year and a half later, more than half the issues created in Linear come from agents. That doesn't mean Linear wants to be a database with an MCP server on top. Cristina thinks SaaS companies settling for that are making a big mistake. If the agent workflows inside your product aren't better than the ones outside it, nobody has a reason to open your app. So she watches two lines: agent usage and app usage. If agent usage climbs and app usage doesn't, you're becoming a commodity. At Linear, both are up and to the right, because people still come back to the app to see and coordinate the work. When Karri published "Issue tracking is dead" in March, most of Linear's customers agreed with him. Then they asked the obvious question: so what am I buying? Linear's answer is a product development system built around agent orchestration, where humans stop doing the manual work of filing, labeling, assigning and closing issues. Customers had been pushing it there. Most of the frontier AI labs run on Linear and wanted it to move faster. Pre-AI companies like Ramp and Coinbase were building their own internal agents and needed an API to plug them into Linear. Cristina says Linear is lucky it's small enough to cannibalize itself. Google has a much harder problem: put an AI answer above every search result, and fewer people look at the ads. Jump to the "issue tracking is dead" discussion → The AI budget behind $100M in months The thing speeding up purchases right now, Cristina says, is AI budget. Companies carved out money for AI tools that didn't exist before, and any product that fits inside it skips the usual fight for spend. At some companies that budget is very high. It's already starting to change. Buyers are signing one-year deals and paid pilots, not three-year contracts, because nobody knows what they'll want in two years. And some overnight-$100M stories are a handful of $30 to $40 million contracts with defense companies or giant law firms. That's a very different business from Linear's 40,000 paying customers on what was, until June, entirely seat-based pricing. When those one-year deals come up for renewal, we'll find out whose ARR was real. Jump to the AI budget discussion → Linear threw out its 2025 enterprise roadmap Three weeks after joining in 2023, Cristina crossed "move upmarket to enterprise" off Linear's company goals. It had one salesperson. She went after growth-stage companies that would have to rip out an existing tool instead, the same way Stripe won new businesses long before it won switchers. Linear finally declared an enterprise push in 2025, with a roadmap full of features for large organizations. Then agents happened. Linear built an MCP server, an agents platform with a whole new set of APIs, and integrations with Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. None of it was planned, and a lot of the enterprise work never got done. Cristina chose to race ahead anyway. Competitors waited, and enterprises started putting Linear on their shortlists. Jump to the enterprise roadmap discussion → No SDRs, no forward deployed engineers Linear has never hired a single SDR. Cristina thinks the qualification call wastes the customer's time: they want a demo, not questions about their budget. AEs do their own outbound, with tooling to keep it personal. It doesn't do forward deployed engineering either. Linear should be easy enough to adopt that nobody needs access to your systems. Solutions engineers sell alongside enterprise AEs instead, sometimes building a working ServiceNow integration overnight to show a prospect it can be done. Cristina adds that an opinionated tool gives agents cleaner data than one where every team defines "bug" differently. Support stays in-house, and Linear won't let an LLM answer tickets on its own. AI drafts replies and a human decides what goes out. Customers sometimes assume the replies are AI because they arrive so fast. In three and a half years, Cristina has never had an escalation over a bad support experience. Jump to the sales team discussion → Everyone wants outcome-based pricing Cristina would love a model like Intercom's Fin, which charges for each support conversation its AI resolves. It's harder for Linear. What is auto-triaging a bug to the right team worth when one company thinks that's the PM's job and another doesn't? Until someone cracks that, Linear charges for what costs it money and keeps the rest free. Seats stay. Linear Agent chat is free even though it runs on frontier models. In coding sessions, users pick OpenAI or Anthropic models and harnesses, and Linear passes through the published API price plus a small markup. Loops run on AI credits. Linear doesn't start charging for things that used to be free. New AI features launch as free betas with notice that pricing is coming, and prices start high and come down rather than the other way around. Jump to the pricing discussion → Cristina says Linear runs on about half the headcount of companies at its stage and revenue. A sales team bigger than the rest of the company would have cost it the trust engineering now has in sales. From Stripe she brought a 40% rule: at least 40% of the company should be engineering, product, design and data. If sales wanted more people, it helped recruit engineers first. Linear has no hard rule, but one of the first things she built was a headcount spreadsheet by function, and she still watches the ratio. Hiring is slow on purpose. Candidates do a work trial on a real problem. Hers was writing Linear's go-to-market plan for the next six to twelve months, which then became her job. At about 170 people, the only C-suite is the founders and her. Jump to the hiring discussion → Linear — the product development system where Cristina is COO. Sharing Linear's growth with the people building it — the August tender at a $2.5 billion valuation, with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention. Issue tracking is dead — Karri's March post on why Linear is building for agents. Linear MCP server — the May 2025 launch Cristina says was basically a first for the category. Introducing Linear Agent — the built-in agent whose chat Linear keeps free.

title: jingyaogong/minimind
abstract:
"大道至簡" 中文 | English 此開源專案旨在完全從 0 開始，僅用 3 塊錢成本與 2 小時訓練時間，即可訓練出規模約為 64M 的超小語言模型 MiniMind。 MiniMind 系列極其輕量，主線最小版本體積約為 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$ ，力求讓普通個人 GPU 也能快速完成訓練與復現。 專案同時開源了大模型的極簡結構與完整訓練鏈路，覆蓋 MoE、資料清洗、預訓練（Pretrain）、監督微調（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等全過程程式碼。 MiniMind 同時拓展了視覺模態模型 MiniMind-V 、多模態 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O 、擴散語言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、線性模型（MiniMind-Linear），詳見 Discussion 。 專案所有核心演算法程式碼均從 0 使用 PyTorch 原生實現，不依賴第三方庫提供的高層抽象介面。 這不僅是一個大語言模型全階段開源復現專案，也是一套面向 LLM 入門與實踐的教程。 希望此專案能為更多人提供一個可復現、可理解、可擴展的起點，一起感受創造的樂趣，並推動更廣泛 AI 社群的進步。 注：本專案基於 Apache 2.0 協議開源，完全免費。“2 小時” 指 SFT 階段在單張 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 1 epoch 的實測耗時，“3 塊錢” 指對應時段的 GPU 租用成本。 🔗 線上體驗 | 🔗 影片介紹 ❤️ 贊助 MiniMind × Infistar.cc ：Claude、GPT、Gemini、DeepSeek等200+模型一個Key搞定，低至官方0.1折（省99%），100%官方純血可驗真，千條線路自動切換。通過 專屬連結 註冊即送¥5。 關於贊助與合作 MiniMind 以 Apache 2.0 協議完全開源、永久免費。贊助完全自願，不換取任何特權，也不影響專案使用。感謝每一位支持者，讓這個業餘時間維護的專案得以持續。 贊助方式包括按月佔位，或直接贊助 GPU 伺服器（算力可能用於專案相關或不相關的研究性探索）。 如有意向，歡迎通過 郵件 聯絡。 📌 專案介紹 大語言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出現，引發了全球範圍內對 AI 的空前關注。無論是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 還是 Qwen，都以驚豔的效果讓人真切感受到這場技術浪潮的衝擊力。然而，動輒數百億參數的模型規模，使得它們對個人裝置而言不僅難以訓練，甚至連部署都顯得遙不可及。開啟大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其內部運作機制，本應是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遺憾的是，絕大多數探索最終都止步於使用 LoRA 等技術對現有大模型做少量微調，學習一些新指令或特定任務。這更像是在教牛頓如何使用 21 世紀的智慧手機——雖然有趣，卻偏離了理解物理本質的初衷。 與此同時，第三方的大模型框架與工具庫，如 transformers / trl / peft 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的介面。只需短短十幾行程式碼，就可以完成“載入模型 + 載入資料集 + 推理 + 強化學習”的全流程訓練。這種高效封裝固然便利，卻也在一定程度上把開發者與底層實現隔離開來，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心程式碼的機會。我認為 “用樂高自己拼出一架飛機，遠比坐在頭等艙裡飛行更讓人興奮”，然而更現實的問題是，網際網路上充斥著大量付費課程和營銷內容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的講解包裝所謂的 AI 教程。正因如此，本專案的初衷就是儘可能降低 LLM 的學習門檻，讓每個人都能從理解每一行程式碼開始，從 0 開始親手訓練一個極小的語言模型。是的，從 零開始訓練 ，而不是僅僅停留在 推理 層面。最低只需不到 3 塊錢的伺服器成本，就能親身體驗從 0 到 1 構建一個語言模型的全過程。 😊 一起感受創造的樂趣吧！ 🎉 本專案包含以下內容 提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 結構程式碼（Dense + MoE），當前主線結構對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態。 提供 Tokenizer 與分詞器訓練程式碼，支援 <tool_call> 、 <tool_response> 、 <think> 等模板標記。 覆蓋 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等完整訓練流程。 提供全階段開源資料，覆蓋收集、蒸餾、清洗與去重後的高質量資料集。 關鍵訓練演算法與核心模組均從 0 實現，不依賴第三方框架封裝。 相容 transformers 、 trl 、 peft 等主流框架，以及 llama.cpp 、 vllm 、 ollama 等常用推理引擎與 Llama-Factory 等訓練框架。 支援單機單卡與單機多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）訓練，支援 wandb / swanlab 視覺化與動態啟停訓練。 支援在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方測評集上進行評測，並支援通過 YaRN 實現 RoPE 長文本外推。 提供相容 OpenAI API 協議的極簡服務端，便於接入 FastGPT、Open-WebUI 等第三方 Chat UI，並支援 reasoning_content 、 tool_calls 、 open_thinking 。 提供基於 Streamlit 的極簡聊天 WebUI，支援思考展示、工具選擇與多輪 Tool Call。 包含實驗性拓展：離散擴散語言模型（ dLM ）與線性注意力模型（ Linear Attention ），均可基於主線 AR 模型進行續訓。 🎉 已釋出模型列表 模型 參數量 Release minimind-3 64M 2026.04.01 minimind-3-moe 198M-A64M 2026.04.01 minimind2-small 26M 2025.04.26 minimind2-moe 145M 2025.04.26 minimind2 104M 2025.04.26 minimind-v1-small 26M 2024.08.28 minimind-v1-moe 4×26M 2024.09.17 minimind-v1 108M 2024.09.01 📝 更新日誌 🔥 2026-04-01 釋出 minimind-3 / minimind-3-moe ：結構、Tokenizer、訓練鏈路、推理介面與預設配置全面更新 結構主線對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態：Dense 約 64M ，MoE 約 198M-A64M ，並移除了 shared expert 設計 預設訓練資料切換為 pretrain_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 sft_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 rlaif.jsonl 、 agent_rl.jsonl 與 agent_rl_math.jsonl 移除獨立 train_reason.py ；思考能力統一由 chat_template + <think> 與 open_thinking 自適應開關控制 toolcall 能力已混入 sft_t2t / sft_t2t_mini 主線資料，預設 full_sft 即具備基礎 Tool Call 能力；同時新增 scripts/chat_api.py 等推理示例 新增原生 Agentic RL 訓練指令碼 train_agent.py ，支援多輪 Tool-Use 場景下的 GRPO / CISPO RLAIF / Agentic RL 訓練流程完成 rollout engine 解耦，支援更靈活地切換生成後端 serve_openai_api.py 與 web_demo.py 新增 reasoning_content / tool_calls / open_thinking 支援 Tokenizer 基於 BPE + ByteLevel 更新，並新增工具呼叫與思考標記，預留 buffer token 便於後續擴展 新增 LoRA 權重合並匯出流程，可通過 scripts/convert_model.py 將基礎模型與 LoRA 權重合併為新的完整模型權重 結構圖資源更新，README 大面積更新 2025-10-24 🔥 新增RLAIF訓練演算法：PPO、GRPO、SPO（從0原生實現） 新增斷點續訓功能：支援訓練自動恢復、跨GPU數量恢復、wandb記錄連續性 新增RLAIF資料集：rlaif-mini.jsonl（從SFT資料隨機取樣1萬條）；簡化DPO資料集，加入中文資料 新增YaRN演算法：支援RoPE長文本外推，提升長序列處理能力 Adaptive Thinking：Reason模型可選是否啟用思考鏈 chat_template全面支援Tool Calling和Reasoning標籤（ <tool_call> 、 <think> 等） 新增RLAIF完整章節、訓練曲線對比、演算法原理摺疊說明 SwanLab 替代WandB（國內訪問友好，API完全相容） 規範化所有程式碼 & 修復一些已知bugs 2025-04-26 重要更新 如有相容性需要，可訪問 🔗舊倉庫內容🔗 。 MiniMind模型參數完全改名，對齊Transformers庫模型（統一命名）。 generate方式重構，繼承自GenerationMixin類。 🔥支援llama.cpp、vllm、ollama等熱門三方生態。 規範程式碼和目錄結構。 改動詞表 <s></s> -> <|im_start|><|im_end|> 為相容第三方推理框架llama.cpp、vllm，本次更新需付出一些可觀代價。
本次更新不再支援「直接」載入25-04-26以前的舊模型進行推理。
由於Llama位置編碼方式與minimind存在區別，導致對映Llama模型後QK值存在差異
minimind2系列舊模型均經過權重對映+（微調訓練）QKVO線性層校準恢復而來。
本次更新後將放棄對`minimind-v1`全系列的維護，並在倉庫中下線。 More... 2025-02-09 迎來發布以來重大更新，Release minimind2 Series。 程式碼幾乎全部重構，使用更簡潔明瞭的統一結構。
如有舊程式碼的相容性需要，可訪問 🔗舊倉庫內容🔗 。 免去資料預處理步驟。統一資料集格式，更換為 jsonl 格式杜絕資料集下載混亂的問題。 minimind2系列效果相比MiniMind-V1顯著提升。 小問題：{kv-cache寫法更標準、MoE的負載均衡loss被考慮等等} 提供模型遷移到私有資料集的訓練方案（醫療模型、自我認知樣例）。 精簡預訓練資料集，並大幅提升預訓練資料質量，大幅縮短個人快速訓練所需時間，單卡3090即可2小時復現！ 更新：LoRA微調脫離peft包裝，從0實現LoRA過程；DPO演算法從0使用PyTorch原生實現；模型白盒蒸餾原生實現。 minimind2-DeepSeek-R1系列蒸餾模型誕生！ minimind2具備一定的英文能力！ 更新minimind2與第三方模型的基於更多大模型榜單測試效能的結果。 2024-10-05 為MiniMind拓展了多模態能力之---視覺 移步孿生專案 minimind-v 檢視詳情！ 2024-09-27 09-27更新pretrain資料集的預處理方式，為了保證文本完整性，放棄預處理成.bin訓練的形式（輕微犧牲訓練速度）。 目前pretrain預處理後的檔案命名為：pretrain_data.csv。 刪除了一些冗餘的程式碼。 2024-09-17 更新minimind-v1-moe模型 為了防止歧義，不再使用mistral_tokenizer分詞，全部採用自定義的minimind_tokenizer作為分詞器。 2024-09-01 更新minimind-v1 (108M)模型，採用minimind_tokenizer，預訓練輪次3 + SFT輪次10，更充分訓練，效能更強。 專案已部署至ModelScope創空間，可以在此網站上體驗： 🔗ModelScope線上體驗🔗 2024-08-27 專案首次開源 📌 快速開始 本人的軟硬體配置（供參考） CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10980XE CPU @ 3.00GHz RAM: 128 GB GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB) * 8 Ubuntu==20.04 CUDA==12.2 Python==3.10.16 requirements.txt 第0步 # 克隆倉庫、安裝依賴 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind cd minimind && pip install -r requirements.txt -i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple Ⅰ 🚀 模型推理 1' 下載模型 在專案根目錄： # 方式1 modelscope download --model gongjy/minimind-3 --local_dir ./minimind-3 # 方式2 git clone https://huggingface.co/jingyaogong/minimind-3 2' CLI 推理 # 方式1：使用 Transformers 格式模型 python eval_llm.py --load_from ./minimind-3 # 方式2：基於 PyTorch 模型（確保./out目錄下有對應權重） python eval_llm.py --load_from ./model --weight full_sft 3'（可選）WebUI # 可能需要`python>=3.10`，安裝 `pip install streamlit` # ⚠️ 須先將 transformers 格式模型資料夾複製到 ./scripts/ 目錄下（例如：cp -r minimind-3 ./scripts/minimind-3），web_demo 指令碼會自動掃描該目錄下包含權重檔案的子資料夾，如不存在則報錯 cd scripts && streamlit run web_demo.py 4'（可選）第三方推理框架 # ollama ollama run jingyaogong/minimind-3 # vllm vllm serve /path/to/model --served-model-name " minimind " Ⅱ 🛠️ 模型訓練 注：提前確認 Torch 的可用後端 import torch print ( torch . cuda . is_available ()) 若你計劃使用 CUDA 訓練，建議先確認當前環境是否已正確識別 GPU。 若 cuda 不可用，也仍可根據自身裝置選擇 CPU 或 MPS 執行，但訓練速度與相容性會有非常大的差異。 如需安裝或更換 PyTorch 版本，可參考 torch_stable 與 連結 1' 下載資料 從下文提供的 資料集下載連結 下載所需資料檔案，並放入 ./dataset 目錄 當前預設僅需下載 pretrain_t2t_mini.jsonl 與 sft_t2t_mini.jsonl ，即可較快復現 MiniMind Zero 對話模型。
如有更多需求，下文提供多種搭配方案，可根據自身任務目標與 GPU 資源靈活選擇。 2' 開始訓練 💡 檢查點暫停續訓 所有訓練指令碼均支援檢查點儲存。新增 --from_resume 1 參數後，即可自動檢測並恢復訓練進度： python train_pretrain.py --from_resume 1
python train_full_sft.py --from_resume 1 # ... 斷點續訓說明： 訓練過程會自動在 ./checkpoints/ 目錄儲存完整檢查點（模型、最佳化器、訓練進度等） 檢查點檔案命名： <權重名>_<維度>_resume.pth （如： full_sft_512_resume.pth ） 支援跨不同 GPU 數量恢復（自動調整 step） 支援 wandb 訓練記錄連續性（自動恢復同一個 run） 適合長時間訓練或不穩定環境，無需擔心訓練中斷導致進度丟失 2.1 預訓練（必須） cd trainer && python train_pretrain.py 訓練後，將得到 out/pretrain_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 * 為模型 dimension，預設為 768 ） 2.2 指令微調（必須） cd trainer && python train_full_sft.py 訓練後，將得到 out/full_sft_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 full 表示全參數微調） 2.3 測試已訓練模型（可選） 確保待測試的模型 *.pth 檔案位於 ./out/ 目錄下；也可直接前往 此處 下載我已訓練好的 *.pth 權重。 python eval_llm.py --weight full_sft --weight 用於指定權重名稱字首，例如 pretrain 、 full_sft 等；更多參數可直接參考 eval_llm.py 注：其它須知 1、所有訓練指令碼均基於 PyTorch 原生實現，並支援多卡加速。 2、若你的裝置有 N (N > 1) 張顯示卡，可通過以下方式啟動單機 N 卡訓練（DDP，也支援擴展到多機多卡）： torchrun --nproc_per_node N train_xxx.py 3、可根據需要開啟 wandb 記錄訓練過程。 ... train_xxx.py --use_wandb 2025 年 6 月後，國內網路環境通常無法直連 WandB。MiniMind 當前預設轉為使用 SwanLab 作為訓練視覺化工具，其介面與 WandB 基本相容；通常只需將 import wandb 替換為 import swanlab as wandb ，其餘呼叫方式基本無需改動。 📌 資料介紹 Ⅰ Tokenizer 分詞器可以粗略理解成 LLM 使用的一本“詞典”，負責把自然語言對映成 token id，再把 token id 解碼迴文本；專案中也提供了 train_tokenizer.py 作為詞表訓練示例。不建議重新訓練 tokenizer，因為詞表和切分規則一旦變化，模型權重、資料格式、推理介面與社群生態的相容性都會下降，也會削弱模型的傳播性。同時，tokenizer 還會影響 PPL 這類按 token 統計的指標，因此跨 tokenizer 比較時，BPB（Bits Per Byte）往往更有參考價值，可參考 這篇 。

Overview vLLM Ascend ( vllm-ascend ) is a community maintained hardware plugin for running vLLM seamlessly on the Huawei Ascend NPU. It is the recommended approach for supporting the Ascend backend within the vLLM community. It adheres to the principles outlined in the [RFC]: Hardware pluggable , providing a hardware-pluggable interface that decouples the integration of the Ascend NPU with vLLM. By using vLLM Ascend plugin, popular open-source models, including Transformer-like, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), Embedding, Multi-modal LLMs can run seamlessly on the Ascend NPU. title: p-e-w/heretic
abstract:
Heretic Training-free language model modification Remove censorship , suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware 1 Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access
to massive computing power usually do: Modify, rather than merely run,
language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses
a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting
example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: Suppress refusals/remove censorship (this is the default action ) Reduce slop ( config.noslop.toml ) Reduce humor ( config.nohumor.toml ) Reduce sycophancy ( config.nosyco.toml ) Alter emotional alignment ( config.emotions.toml ) Shorten response length ( config.terse.toml ) and many, many other things. ‼️ Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally ‼️ In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model in a matter of seconds . Heretic supports most dense models, including
many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern
hybrid models. The community has created and published thousands of models with Heretic.
Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics
like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models
produced with competing abliteration tools. 2 3 Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate
for your hardware. Then run: pip install -U heretic-llm
heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Replace Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with whatever model you want to process. By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression). If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked
above, or write your own. See config.default.toml for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from config.toml in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE environment variable. Important Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are not compatible with Heretic 2.x!
See the migration guide for what you need to change
in order to make your old configurations work. At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine
the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware.
On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 takes about 30-40 minutes. After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to
save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works,
run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions. Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are
computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full
control over what Heretic does to models. The Scorer interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from
is defined in scorer.py . The only required method
is get_score , but there is more machinery (such as settings management)
available when you need it. By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in keyword_rate.py ) and KL divergence
(implemented in kl_divergence.py ).
Additional scorers are available in the scorers directory .
These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily
be adapted to your needs. Scorers are configured through the main configuration file .
Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the scorers setting, which
also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during
optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores
will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured
with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation
of this mechanism. The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import
path ( fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass ) or as a file path followed by
a class name ( path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass ). You do not have to modify
the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins. Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in the next section . How Heretic works Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in modifier.py ) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer
powered by Optuna . The optimizer finds a set of parameters that,
when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model ( see above ). Heretic ships with two modifiers: Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA) 4 : This is the default modifier, and was
specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA
works in the original pull request ,
and see the precise implementation in ara.py . Directional ablation aka "abliteration" 5 : The classic method for refusal
suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over
the layers, and supports both projected abliteration 6 and norm preservation (MPOA) 7 .
The complete code is in abliteration.py . You can use the modifiers setting to switch between modifier implementations.
Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows
only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future. Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire Heretic has the ability to create reproducible models whose repositories contain
all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand,
provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch
doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers,
operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions
are exactly the same. Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to
Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely
optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a reproduce folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model
( example ).
This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest
file named reproduce.json , which includes all the information Heretic needs to automatically reproduce the model. Automatic reproduction can be performed with heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one
that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches.
The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do not have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you
have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files
against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical,
depending on how closely your system resembles the original one). Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face.
Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests
form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will. That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it here . But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the
library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a distributed system,
and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from
Hugging Face whenever you want by running heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/ You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued.
To update this collection, simply run the command again.

title: colbymchenry/codegraph
abstract:
CodeGraph Already installed? Run codegraph upgrade Follow @getcodegraph on X for updates. Supercharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Gemini, Antigravity, Kiro, GitHub Copilot, and more with Semantic Code Intelligence The fastest complete code graph · surgical context · built for how agents actually work · 100% local **Kernel powered by Rust** Documentation & Website → The CodeGraph platform is coming — for every PR, know exactly what to test, what could break, which flows are affected, and whether business logic is compromised. Get early beta access to the hosted product · getcodegraph.com Contents Get Started Language Support Why CodeGraph? Key Features Framework-aware Routes Mixed iOS / React Native / Expo bridging Quick Start How It Works CLI Reference MCP Tools Library Usage Configuration Telemetry Verified releases Supported Platforms Supported Agents Supported Languages Measured cross-file coverage Troubleshooting Contributing License Get Started 1. Install the CLI No Node.js required — one command grabs the right build for your OS: # macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh # Windows (PowerShell) irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.ps1 | iex Already have Node? Use npm instead (works on any version) npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph CodeGraph bundles its own runtime — nothing to compile, no native build, works the same everywhere. The installer puts codegraph on your PATH but doesn't change your current shell — open a new terminal before the next step so the command resolves. Upgrade any time with codegraph upgrade — it detects how you installed (bundle, npm, or npx) and updates in place. Add --check to see if an update is available, or codegraph upgrade <version> to pin one. After an upgrade, codegraph status and your agent tell you when a project's index was built by an older version: run codegraph index there to rebuild it. 2. Wire up your agent(s) In a new terminal , run the installer to connect CodeGraph to the agents you use: codegraph install Detects and auto-configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Hermes Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity IDE, Kiro, GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI, JetBrains IDEs), IBM Bob, Factory Droid, Windsurf, Qwen Code, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Kimi Code, Qoder CLI, and Pi — wiring the CodeGraph MCP server into each. This is the step that connects CodeGraph to your agent; installing the CLI in step 1 does not do it on its own. It only wires up your agent — it does not index any code; building each project's graph is the separate codegraph init in step 3. (Shortcut: npx @colbymchenry/codegraph downloads and runs this in one go.) 3. Initialize each project cd your-project
codegraph init codegraph init creates the local .codegraph/ directory and builds the full graph in the same step — one command, done. 4. No more syncing! Auto-sync is enabled by default. CodeGraph watches the project and updates the graph on every file change — while your agent edits code, or you add, modify, or delete files. The index is never stale, and there is nothing to re-run. Uninstall Changed your mind? One command removes CodeGraph from every agent it configured and the CLI itself — every install it finds (standalone bundle, npm global package, launcher link), shown to you before anything is deleted: codegraph uninstall Pass --keep-cli to remove only the agent configurations and keep the CLI installed. Reverses the installer — strips CodeGraph's MCP server config, instructions, and permissions from each configured agent. Your project indexes ( .codegraph/ ) are left untouched; remove those per-project with codegraph uninit . Use --target to remove from specific agents, or --yes to run non-interactively. Language Support Every language below gets the same treatment — full structural extraction and cross-file resolution into one graph, no per-language setup: Per-language details — extensions, frameworks, and what exactly gets extracted — in Supported Languages . Why CodeGraph? When an AI agent needs to understand code — to answer a question or make a change — it discovers structure the slow way: grep, glob, and Read, one file at a time, rebuilding call paths and dependencies by hand. That's a pile of tool calls and round-trips before it even starts the real work. CodeGraph hands the agent the exact code it needs in one call. It's a pre-built knowledge graph of every symbol, call edge, and dependency in your codebase — so instead of crawling files, the agent asks one question and gets back the relevant source, the call paths between those symbols (including dynamic-dispatch hops grep can't follow), and the blast radius of a change. Surgical context, not a file-by-file search — which means fewer tool calls and faster answers on every codebase, large or small. A note on cost: CodeGraph's win on every codebase is precision — the agent stops crawling files and answers from the graph. On current models that precision is also a large direct saving: the 2026-08 re-measurement, on a harness that blocks the CLI in both arms, put it at 44% lower cost and 62% fewer tokens on average across the seven benchmark repos, because a strong model without the graph burns its budget re-deriving structure. Cost tracks how much discovery a question demands more than raw repo size: 57–78% on questions the file-reading agent needed 28–43 tool calls to answer, near-even where it got there in 7. A note on context: the numbers above measure throughput — tokens processed, tools called, dollars spent to reach one answer. They don't measure what is still sitting in your context window afterward, and on that axis CodeGraph costs more , not less. Across the same seven repos in multi-turn sessions, CodeGraph's responses leave about 80% more retrieval context resident at the end of a session than a file-reading agent's do — on VS Code, 67k tokens against 18k. The mechanism is the same one that makes it fast: CodeGraph returns one dense, verbatim payload that answers the question and then stays in the window, where a grep-and-read agent churns through many small results that get evicted. Fewer tokens processed and a larger persistent footprint are both real at once. If you run long sessions in a small window, budget for it. Measured per-repo: docs/benchmarks/residual-context-occupancy.md . Benchmark Results Tested across 7 real-world open-source codebases spanning 7 languages, comparing an agent (Claude Code, headless) answering one architecture question with and without CodeGraph, at the median of 4 runs per arm . Re-measured 2026-08-05 on Claude Opus 4.8 against the current build, on a harness that blocks the codegraph CLI in both arms — contamination row: 0 of 28 without-arm runs. The universal win — every repo, every size: 88% fewer tool calls · 53% faster · 62% fewer tokens · 44% cheaper · file reads cut to zero on all seven repos. With the index available, the agent answers from one to four codegraph_explore calls and stops. Without it, the agent burns its budget on discovery — up to 43 tool calls and 19 file reads re-deriving what the graph already knew. Every repo was faster with CodeGraph in this measurement — by 35% on the narrowest question, by 3.6× on the widest. Codebase Language Tool calls Time File reads Tokens Cost VS Code TypeScript · ~11k files 2 vs 28 2.2× faster (58s vs 2m 10s) 0 vs 12 77% fewer 71% cheaper Excalidraw TypeScript · ~640 2 vs 43 3.6× faster (45s vs 2m 42s) 0 vs 18 84% fewer 78% cheaper Django Python · ~3k 3 vs 14 35% faster (54s vs 1m 23s) 0 vs 8.5 41% fewer 13% cheaper¹ Tokio Rust · ~790 3 vs 29 2.6× faster (1m 3s vs 2m 43s) 0 vs 19 65% fewer 64% cheaper OkHttp Java · ~645 1 vs 6 43% faster (33s vs 58s) 0 vs 2 54% fewer 21% cheaper Gin Go · ~110 1 vs 7 39% faster (28s vs 46s) 0 vs 4 52% fewer ~even¹ Alamofire Swift · ~110 4 vs 33 2.6× faster (54s vs 2m 22s) 0 vs 16.

title: louis-e/arnis
abstract:
Arnis Arnis creates complex and accurate Minecraft Java Edition (1.21.4+), Bedrock Edition, Luanti (Minetest) and Hytale worlds that reflect real-world geography, topography, and architecture. This free and open source project is designed to handle large-scale geographic data from the real world and generate detailed Minecraft worlds. The algorithm processes geospatial data from OpenStreetMap as well as elevation data to create an accurate Minecraft representation of terrain and architecture.
Generate your hometown, big cities, and natural landscapes with ease! Want mobile generation or larger map sizes? MapSmith generates worlds in your browser, no install required. This GitHub page and arnismc.com are the only official project websites. Do not download Arnis from any other website. ⌨️ Usage Download the latest release or compile the project on your own. Choose your area on the map using the rectangle tool, then simply click on Start Generation !
Additionally, you can customize various generation settings, such as world scale, spawn point, or building interior generation. 📚 Documentation Full documentation is available in the GitHub Wiki , covering topics such as generation settings, command line usage, technical explanations, FAQs and contribution guidelines. backgroundvid.webm 🏆 Open Source Key objectives of this project Modularity : Ensure that all components (e.g., data fetching, processing, and world generation) are cleanly separated into distinct modules for better maintainability and scalability. Performance Optimization : We aim to maintain strong performance and fast world generation. Comprehensive Documentation : Detailed in-code documentation for a clear structure and logic. User-Friendly Experience : Focus on making the project easy to use for end users. Cross-Platform Support : We want this project to run smoothly on Windows, macOS, and Linux. How to contribute This project is open source and welcomes contributions from everyone! Whether you're interested in fixing bugs, improving performance, adding new features, or enhancing documentation, your input is valuable. Simply fork the repository, make your changes, and submit a pull request. Please respect the above-mentioned key objectives. Contributions of all levels are appreciated, and your efforts help improve this tool for everyone. Command line Build: cargo run --release --no-default-features -- --output-dir="C:/YOUR_PATH/.minecraft/saves" --bbox="min_lat,min_lng,max_lat,max_lng" GUI Build: cargo run --release All command line options, like the generation modes, winter and One World, are explained on the Command Line Usage wiki page. After your pull request is merged, I will take care of regularly creating update releases which will include your changes. If you are using Nix, you can run the program directly with nix run github:louis-e/arnis -- --output-dir=YOUR_PATH/.minecraft/saves --bbox="min_lat,min_lng,max_lat,max_lng" ⭐ Star History 📰 Academic & Press Recognition Arnis has been recognized in various academic and press publications after gaining more attention in December 2024. Building realistic Minecraft worlds with Open Data on AWS: How Arnis uses elevation datasets at scale Floodcraft: Game-based Interactive Learning Environment using Minecraft for Flood Mitigation and Preparedness for K-12 Education Hackaday: Bringing OpenStreetMap Data into Minecraft TomsHardware: Minecraft Tool Lets You Create Scale Replicas of Real-World Locations XDA Developers: Hometown Minecraft Map: Arnis Free to use press assets, including screenshots and logos, can be found here . 🔒 Code Signing Policy Free code signing provided by SignPath.io , certificate by SignPath Foundation . title: Spending 35B Opus 5.5 Tokens to Write a Symphony
Bare Metal Qwen
abstract:
Phase 2: Bare-Metal Bootable Qwen3-0.6B OS in 24 KB of Pure Assembly A standalone bootable x86-64 operating system that runs Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B directly on hardware or KVM with no Linux, no Windows, no C, no Rust, and no libc . 24,252 bytes stripped static Multiboot 1 kernel ( FAST_Q8=1 , default: .text = 17,143 B, .rodata = 2,772 B, .bss = 2.1 MiB NOBITS , zero dynamic dependencies), or 23,612 bytes ( FAST_Q8=0 , legacy Q8_0xFP32). 74–94 ms cold boot to interactive asm-llm> multi-turn chat with persistent KV-cache across turns, all SMP cores online, and the .asmbin v2 ( 614 MiB FP16 scales) or v1 ( 649 MiB FP32 scales) model bound zero-copy from physical RAM on 2 MiB huge pages. 100% token-exact and byte-for-byte parity with Phase 1 across 1..32 vCPUs. 134.9 tok/s decode on QEMU KVM (AMD EPYC 7642, 16 vCPUs; 23.7 tok/s at 1 vCPU, 118.1 tok/s at 8 vCPUs, 136.6 tok/s peak) and 55.4 tok/s live on a 0 GB disk Proxmox VE VM (Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 12 cores). Running live on a diskless ( 0 GB storage) Proxmox VE VM booted from the hybrid BIOS+UEFI ISO (Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 12 cores, 2 GiB RAM): Prerequisites x86-64 CPU with AVX2 + FMA + F16C . Core build & QEMU KVM: sudo apt install nasm binutils qemu-system-x86 Optional, for building a bootable BIOS+UEFI hybrid ISO ( make os-iso ): sudo apt install grub-pc-bin grub-efi-amd64-bin grub-common mtools xorriso An exported models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin file ( --scale-dtype fp16 v2 recommended, or legacy v1 --scale-dtype fp32 ; see Phase 1 setup ). Build From the repository root ( FAST_Q8=1 is enabled by default; pass FAST_Q8=0 for legacy FP32-activation mode): make os FAST_Q8=1
make os-check Expected output ( FAST_Q8=1 ): -rwxr-xr-x 1 user user 24252 build/asm-llm-os.elf
build/asm-llm-os.elf: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped
There is no dynamic section in this file. (The kernel is linked as 64-bit ELF and wrapped into ELF32 via objcopy -O elf32-i386 for standard Multiboot 1 loaders like QEMU -kernel and GRUB2; boot.asm transitions immediately into 64-bit Long Mode.) Running & Deploying Option A: Instant QEMU KVM Boot (~85 ms) Boot directly in the terminal over COM1 serial ( -nographic ): qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -kernel build/asm-llm-os.elf \ -initrd models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin \ -nographic Or use the Makefile shortcut: make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16 Run a one-shot batch prompt with clean ACPI shutdown: make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16 \ CMDLINE= ' prompt="Explain how a CPU cache works in 3 concise sentences." max_tokens=64 think=0 shutdown=1 ' Open a live 80x25 VGA GUI window with PS/2 keyboard input: qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -kernel build/asm-llm-os.elf \ -initrd models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin \ -vga std -serial stdio Option B: Bootable Hybrid BIOS+UEFI ISO Packages the 23 KB kernel, GRUB2 Multiboot 1 config, and the 649 MiB .asmbin model into a single self-contained ~661 MiB bootable ISO ( build/asm-llm-os.iso ): make os-iso MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin Boot the ISO in QEMU KVM (SeaBIOS or UEFI OVMF): # Legacy BIOS (SeaBIOS) qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -cdrom build/asm-llm-os.iso -nographic # UEFI (OVMF) qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -bios /usr/share/ovmf/OVMF.fd \ -cdrom build/asm-llm-os.iso -nographic Option C: Deploying on Proxmox VE (0 GB Disk VM) Because the entire OS and model live inside the ISO and run out of RAM, the VM needs zero hard disks . Upload build/asm-llm-os.iso to your Proxmox node's ISO storage ( local -> ISO Images -> Upload , or scp into /var/lib/vz/template/iso/asm-llm-os.iso ). Create and start a diskless VM on the Proxmox host (pick an unused <vmid> , e.g. 250 ): qm create 250 \ --name asm-llm-os \ --machine pc \ --bios seabios \ --cpu host \ --cores 12 \ --memory 2048 \ --balloon 0 \ --vga std \ --serial0 socket \ --ide2 local:iso/asm-llm-os.iso,media=cdrom \ --boot order=ide2 qm start 250 Interact either through the Proxmox web UI ( noVNC Console , VGA + PS/2 keyboard) or over the virtual serial port: qm terminal 250 (Note: --cpu host is required so the VM exposes AVX2 + FMA, and --balloon 0 ensures 2 GiB of contiguous guest RAM for the 649 MiB model + 449 MiB KV-cache arena.) Interactive Multi-Turn Chat & Kernel Cmdline Interactive Console ( asm-llm> ) By default, the bare-metal console runs in multi-turn chat mode with persistent KV-cache : each new user turn prefills only the new Qwen3 chat tokens starting at g_chat_pos without recomputing earlier turns, closes every assistant turn in the KV-cache with <|im_end|>\n , and displays live context usage ( ctx=X/2048 ) in the decode stats line. title: Why aren't we working 2-days a week?
abstract:
Okay, AI is here to replace us. At this point the dream is that corporations save billions through layoffs, productivity gains and increasing the precarity of the existing workers, while a few people at AI companies profit from the technology and the hype. There are AI tools being baked into every process whether they work or not and the hocus-pocus words of the hours automation, knowledge work, singularity and efficiency. So why is everyone in white collar jobs still working 40+ hour days as the norm? Why aren't these productivity gains being passed on to the employees who can in turn use it for leisure or whatever it is that they fancy? Rather with the advent of AI, the focus seems to be working more. Jobs are slashed and the existing workers take the work of more people for the same pay and even more precarious conditions. At some point there needs to be a bigger talk about the societal impact of AI and how it should lead to more free time if not less. The times of factory work and the mandated 5 day work weeks feel archaic in this new paradigm, less commutes, lesser pollution offsetting for the greater energy consumption from the datacenters. Let the rich get rich and the poor have fun, let laziness roost and 21st century be one of rest and relaxation. # AI # leisure # workweek
